title: Sunset Session

conditions.headline: Split Peaks: Dow Wipes Out, Nasdaq Catches a Ride
conditions.summary: The Dow fell 1.1% as managed care and energy sank and hawkish Fed minutes weighed, while the Nasdaq rose 0.4% to end a four-day skid. The S&P 500 slipped 0.2% for a fifth straight loss.

sections.title: Closing Bell
items: Dow fell 561 points (-1.1%) to 50,198; S&P 500 slipped 0.2% to 7,324; Nasdaq rose 0.4% to 24,430; Russell 2000 gained about 0.5%.
The S&P 500 posted its fifth straight loss, its longest losing streak since June, while the Nasdaq ended a four-day skid.
The Dow was down more than 600 points at its lows before trimming losses late.
Hawkish Fed minutes, a second day of managed-care selling and an energy slide weighed; cybersecurity and some tech names held up.
Energy was the weakest sector, and health insurers were the Dow's biggest drag; small caps outperformed.

sections.title: Macro & Fed
items: October FOMC minutes: almost all officials saw further rate hikes as likely appropriate; a couple were open to a half-point move in December.
Fed Governor Waller said a half-point hike is probably needed at the Dec. 8-9 meeting; futures lean toward a quarter-point hike.
October housing starts rose 9.9% to 1.309 million, beating 1.23 million expected; permits fell to 1.295 million vs. 1.378 million expected.
Pending home sales fell 4.7% in October vs. -2.0% expected, to a record-low index level.

10-year yield eased about 4 basis points to 5.07%; the dollar touched a 19-month high; WTI fell 3.2% to $83.26 after a 3.4M-barrel crude build; gold fell about 3% to near $3,740; bitcoin dropped to about $62,450.

sections.title: Biggest Movers
items: PANW (Palo Alto Networks): +9.9% — cybersecurity rally ahead of results; SentinelOne and CrowdStrike also jumped.
BRBR (BellRing Brands): +24.1% — quarterly sales up 7% and upbeat fiscal 2027 guidance.
TTWO (Take-Two Interactive): +8.4% — rally ahead of Thursday's GTA VI launch.
TJX (TJX Companies): +8.0% — comparable sales up 4% and solid holiday guidance.
UNH (UnitedHealth): -10.2% — managed-care selloff over a proposed Medicare Advantage audit crackdown.
HUM (Humana): -13.0% — same Medicare Advantage pressure on insurers.
JMIA (Jumia): -40.6% — cut its full-year outlook on weak Black Friday sales.
NVDA (Nvidia): -2.9% — gave up early gains despite revenue doubling to $115.8 billion.

sections.title: Earnings Today & Tonight
items: Target (before open): comparable sales up 5.6% and a raised sales outlook; shares rose about 4%.
TJX (before open): comps up 4%, EPS of $1.39; shares rose 8%.
Lowe's (before open): topped estimates and kept its outlook, but shares were weaker.
Palo Alto Networks (after close): revenue up 39% to $3.44 billion, raised full-year guidance and agreed to buy Applied Compute for $4.5 billion in stock; shares up about 6.5% after hours.
Nvidia (reported Tuesday): Q3 revenue rose 103% to $115.8 billion with a roughly $130 billion Q4 outlook, but the stock fell 2.9%.

sections.title: Business News
items: Anthropic's IPO is expected to price tonight and begin trading Thursday on Nasdaq under ANT, with reports of demand above the $70-$78 range.
Textron agreed to sell its industrial unit to Kingswood Capital for $1.2 billion in cash.
Pfizer struck a licensing deal with Starna including $330 million upfront.
Federal regulators' proposed Medicare Advantage audit rule kept pressure on health insurers for a second day.
Nvidia is operating under interim CEO Colette Kress after Jensen Huang's departure.

sections.title: On Deck
items: 7:30 AM CT: weekly jobless claims and the Philadelphia Fed manufacturing index.
9:00 AM CT: Census advance Q3 services report.
Before the open: Walmart, Alibaba and Williams-Sonoma report earnings.
Anthropic (ANT) is expected to make its Nasdaq debut; GTA VI launches.
The Fed's next decision comes at the Dec. 8-9 meeting.
